name: Swiss rail timetable
thesis: A public timetable's discipline: a strict grid, tabular numerals, arrows and no decoration. Trust comes from legibility under time pressure.
risk: Reads cold; warmth has to come from type and photography, never ornament.

name: Risograph zine
thesis: Two spot inks, visible halftone and deliberate misregistration make a small budget look like a scene.
risk: Misregistration eats small text; body copy stays on one ink.

name: Admiralty chart
thesis: Depth contours, sounding numbers and magenta corrections turn dense data into a navigable surface.
risk: Dense notation intimidates; it needs one clear legend and a scale it never betrays.

name: Library card catalogue
thesis: Index cards, typewriter type and ruled lines: an interface that explains itself by looking like its own record.
risk: Nostalgia without function; every card must carry real data.

name: Aeroplane safety card
thesis: Flat pictograms in sequence, no words needed: the most compressed instruction set in the world.
risk: Reduction can drop nuance the task actually needs.

name: Museum wall label
thesis: Small caps, a generous margin and one object per field of view; the interface gets out of the work's way.
risk: Too quiet for a page that has to sell something.

name: Seed catalogue
thesis: Engraved illustration, a sturdy serif and dense captions: commerce that reads like a reference book.
risk: Illustration is the cost; a weak one sinks the whole page.

name: Departure board
thesis: Flip-board rows, one fact per column, numerals that align: scanning beats reading.
risk: A grid of rows flattens hierarchy if every row looks alike.

name: Surveyor's field book
thesis: Pencil rules, marginal notes and coordinates: the look of evidence that work was actually done.
risk: Hand-made marks become decoration when nothing is measured.

name: Banknote engraving
thesis: Guilloche patterns, a portrait and a restrained palette: authority built from craft rather than colour.
risk: Ornament without a reason is pastiche.

name: Lab notebook
thesis: Graph paper, ink entries and a stamped date: a record that expects to be checked.

name: Theatre playbill
thesis: Wood type stacked to fill the sheet, names in rank order: hierarchy you can read across a street.

name: Transit map
thesis: Colour-coded lines at 45 degrees and stations as ticks: topology over geography.
risk: A diagram can hide the distances users actually care about.

name: Trade catalogue
thesis: A product grid, spec tables and a hard price column: utility as the aesthetic.
risk: Tables full of filler read as filler.

name: Observatory almanac
thesis: Tables, star charts and a sober serif: prediction presented as a public service.
risk: Table-heavy pages break on small screens unless the table is designed to move.

name: Repair manual
thesis: Exploded diagrams with numbered callouts and short imperative sentences.
risk: Callouts without a real diagram are lies.

name: Ticket roll
thesis: A narrow column of monospaced lines, perforated edges and a total at the bottom: every row is a transaction.
risk: Monotony makes the one exceptional row invisible.

name: Botanical plate
thesis: Fine line work, Latin labels and one specimen per sheet: precision as the visual language.
risk: Fine line disappears on low-density screens.
